 Nation issues more than 500 new membership ID cards since September
 The new cards are TSA-compliant, expire every five years and will eventually be required to access Nation programs and services.
 By Collyn Combs - October 23, 2026 0 
 You can now apply for a new Osage Nation Membership ID card. ECHO REED/Osage News Facebook X Pinterest Linkedin 
 The Osage Nation Membership Department has been busy, issuing new membership photo ID cards to the nearly 27,000 enrolled citizens.
 Since Sept. 1, the Membership Department has processed more than 500 new membership ID cards. While the new membership ID cards aren’t required for Nation services just yet, they will be in the future.
 “At some point, all these different departments across Osage Nation are going to require this membership ID,” said Membership Department Director Chris Standingbear. “The new membership ID does have an expiration date, and it’s five years. I can’t say for sure, but approximately a year from now, constituents are going to start seeing these different programs require a valid Osage Nation membership ID card, which means the new card with a photo and signature, and it has to be current.”
 The new membership ID cards are also REAL ID compliant.
 “The addition of an expiration date creates an important opportunity to maintain current constituent contact information, allowing departments to communicate more effectively and deliver programs, services, and benefits in a more targeted and efficient manner,” said ON Secretary of Administration Susan Bayro. “By providing a TSA-compliant Membership ID Card, the Osage Nation retains ownership and management of member information rather than relying on state systems. In addition, the card is provided to members at no cost, eliminating the need for members to obtain and pay for a state-issued REAL ID in order to meet TSA identification requirements.”
 Eventually, to access services through the membership portal, constituents will be required to upload their membership ID card.
 Osage News Reporter Collyn Combs receives her new membership ID card. ECHO REED/Osage News 
 How to apply 
 Constituents can apply for the new membership ID card at the Membership Department office in Pawhuska or online via the Osage Nation portal .
 There is no cost to apply for a membership ID card initially, but replacements or renewals cost $20 each. The ID cards must be renewed every five years.
 “People can walk in and have it done here, but we actually prefer that people utilize the Osage Nation service portal,” said Standingbear. “There’s a module on there for the membership ID card and it’s super simple. You fill in the application, the online form in the portal, and it’s just your basic information: your name, your address, your physical traits, your traits like height and weight, eye color, etc.”
 Constituents can upload their photo and signature from their phone and submit it, and the Membership Department will mail the new card out once it’s processed and ready.
 “We’ve actually had more people using the portal than we have walk-ins, which is good because we only have so much capacity here at the office and there’s 27,000 members,” Standingbear said.
 If applying for a membership ID card through the portal, the photo must be in color, with no glasses, selfies, Photoshop, or filters; the background must be white or off-white; and it must be a clear image taken in the last six months. The requirements are similar to those for a passport photo ID.
 Constituents applying for a membership ID card in person will have their photo taken at the office. If there’s no wait, the process takes about 5 to 10 minutes.
 The photo ID has the same features as the previous cards, but it now includes the cardholder’s height, weight, hair and eye color, and physical address. The back also includes a QR code so constituents can access the portal.
 Osage designer Blake Cunningham worked on the graphics and format for the new ID cards, which have been in the works for several years.
 Minors don’t need a photo or signature on their ID cards unless they want one; however, everyone 18 and older must have a photo and a signature.
 “This project represents a major advancement in service delivery, data accuracy, member convenience, and Osage Nation self-determination,” Bayro said. “I am extremely proud of my team’s dedication and perseverance in bringing this long-standing initiative to completion.”

 Previous article Nearly five years after purchase, Lost Creek Ranch still lacks finalized plan Collyn Combs https://osagenews.org Collyn Combs is a graduate of Oklahoma State University with a Bachelor of Science in multimedia journalism. She is a member of the Osage Nation and a descendant of original allottee Alice Mosier Riddle Stobaugh. Her family is from the Grayhorse district. 
Combs is from Ponca City, Oklahoma and attended school in Bartlesville, Oklahoma, where she graduated in 2017. She served on the newspaper staff at Bartlesville High School from 2016-2017. 
She attended Northern Oklahoma College in Tonkawa after graduation and wrote for “The Maverick” newspaper from 2017-2020 and served as editor from 2018-2019. She also served as the reporter for “Northern Thunder.” 
An avid lover of weather, she helped relaunch the O’Colly TV weather program and served as meteorologist from 2022-2024; she was involved with the Omega Phi Alpha National service sorority from 2023-2024 and served as secretary and membership chairs and was involved with the Native American Student Association. 
She has freelanced for Osage News for two years and completed an internship with the Osage Nation Education Department . She was also a recipient of the Osage Nation Higher Education Scholarship . 
Combs was recently confirmed as a board member for the Osage County Historical Society .
